question: In the Li3PO4-coated NCM study, how much did the charge-transfer resistance rise over 50 cycles for the bare and the coated material, and what capacity did each retain after 100 cycles at 1C?
rendered:
The charge-transfer resistance (Rct) for the bare NCM material increased from 27.99 to 224.04 Ω over 50 cycles, whereas for the Li3PO4-coated NCM material it only increased from 14.88 to 144.75 Ω.

After 100 cycles at 1C, the bare NCM material retained 75.4% of its initial discharge capacity, whereas the Li3PO4-coated NCM material retained 88.4%.
